runner.text:
**Brief for the coach — what the last check found**

**What was done.** I searched the engine's working files to see where the plate-loading calculator (the web tool the athlete uses to work out which plates to put on the bar) is referenced, and which ready-made "load this weight" links the engine has already written out. This was a read-only look-up. Nothing was changed, nothing was recorded, and there is nothing for the athlete to agree to.

**Where the calculator is referenced.** It appears in the coach settings, the athlete's profile, the athlete's summary page, the home-kit description (the kit labelled as the "achievable" home set-up), and in six routines: Sunday deadlift, daily hang, conditioning circuit, Monday overhead press, Saturday bench, and Friday squat. So every main lifting day plus the hang and conditioning work is wired to it.

**The pre-built loading links found.** Each of these is a one-click link that opens the calculator with a target weight already filled in, using the home kit's inventory:

- Barbell at **140.5 lb**, secured with collar clamps.
- Barbell at **55.5 lb**, secured with collar clamps.
- Dumbbell at **32.5 lb**, using the standard screw-on collars.
- Dumbbell at **5 lb**, with no collar hardware at all.
- Dumbbell at **20 lb**, using the standard screw-on collars. This exact link appears twice, so two different places in the plan point to the same 20 lb dumbbell load.
- Kettlebell at **40 lb**, using the standard screw-on collars.

There are also at least three copies of a "set up the home kit" link, which pre-loads the full inventory of plates, bars, dumbbell handles and kettlebell handle into the calculator so the athlete only has to do that once per device.

**What the half-pound figures mean.** The 140.5 lb and 55.5 lb barbell targets are not round numbers on purpose: they already account for the weight of the bar and the collar clamps, so the calculator will show exactly which plates to add to arrive at that total. The athlete should not round them up or down themselves — just open the link and load what it shows.

**Warnings.** None. The search returned no errors or flags, so there is nothing blocking training and nothing to clear.

**Proposed changes.** None were made or suggested. If the athlete wants a loading link for any other weight, that would be a new request; nothing is pending their approval right now.

**One caveat.** The results were cut off near the end of the list (a few hundred characters were not shown), so there may be one further loading link I could not read. If you want certainty on that last entry, say so and I will pull the remainder.

first.text:

What I didn't get back was the address itself in a form I can hand you — the lookup described where the link lives and what it does, but didn't surface the actual URL text. I don't want to guess at it and send you to the wrong place.

What I did see are the ready-made loading links already built for you, each opening the calculator with your home kit and a target weight filled in:

- Barbell at 140.5 lb (with clamps)
- Barbell at 55.5 lb (with clamps)
- Dumbbell at 32.5 lb
- Dumbbell at 20 lb (used in two places)
- Dumbbell at 5 lb (no collars)
- Kettlebell at 40 lb

Plus a "set up the home kit" link that loads your plates, bars and handles into the calculator once per device. The half-pound barbell targets are deliberate — they already include bar and clamp weight, so just load what the calculator shows rather than rounding.

Want me to go back and pull the actual link out for you? One more pass and I'll have it.
